html:
The Vakatakas ruled much of the Deccan in central India from the mid 3rd century to around 500, after the Satavahanas and alongside the Gupta Empire to their north.

The dynasty was founded by Vindhyashakti, and his son Pravarasena I was the only Vakataka to take the title of emperor. The family soon split into two branches. The Guptas treated the Vakatakas as key allies: Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavatigupta to a Vakataka king, and she ruled as regent for her young sons.

Their great legacy is art. Under King Harishena in the late 5th century, ministers and nobles paid for most of the Buddhist caves and wall paintings at Ajanta; see the Ajanta cave paintings. The dynasty faded soon after his death, and its lands passed to new powers such as the Chalukyas and the Vishnukundinas.
sum: The Vakatakas ruled much of the Deccan in central India from the mid 3rd century to around 500, after the Satavahanas and alongside the Gupta Empire to their north.
